technical-data.invention-title: BETON RENFERMANT UN SUPERPLASTIFIANT ET UNE PALYGORSKITE

nplcit.text: DATABASE WPI Week 198907, Derwent Publications Ltd., London, GB; AN 1989-051918, XP002947499 & JP 64 003 040 A (DENKI KAGAKU KOGYO KK) 06 January 1989 & PATENT ABSTRACTS OF JAPAN & JP 64 003 040 A (DENKI KAGAKU KOGYO KK) 06 January 1989

abstract.p: Concept for a self-compacting, self-levelling High Performance Concrete by addition of 2-10 % palygorskite with an aspect ratio (length:diameter) of more than 35. The addition of palygorskite in combination with a superplasticiser lends itself to control of the ratio between viscosity and yield strength of the fresh concrete. Good visco-elastic properties, which assure high filling capacity, good flow properties and stability of the microstructure are obtained through this concept. Concrete produced in accordance with this invention is particularly characterised by its self-compacting properties, its filling capacity and its high stability during pumping even at high pumping pressures of 100 to 200 bars.

L'invention concerne un béton haute performance d'auto-compactage et d'auto nivellement obtenu par addition d'environ 2 à 10 % de palygorskite dont le rapport de forme (longueur:diamètre) est supérieur à 35. L'addition de palygorskite alliée à un superplastifiant permet de contrôler le rapport entre la viscosité et la limite de rupture du béton frais. C'est par ce biais que l'on garantit de bonnes propriétés viscoélastiques assurant une forte capacité de remplissage, un bon écoulement et une stabilité de la microstructure. Le béton, obtenu selon cette invention, est caractérisé par ses propriétés d'auto-compactage, sa capacité de remplissage et sa forte stabilité en cours de pumping et ce, même à des pressions élevées de pumping allant de 100 à 200 bars.

description.p: GENERAL DESCRIPTION
Title of invention CONCRETE CONTAINING SUPERPLASTICISER AND PALYGORSKITE
Scope of invention
Production of concrete, including concrete structures characteπsed by High Performance, e g enhanced service lifetime, high strength, high resistance towards environmental exposure
BACKGROUND
In modern High Strength/High Performance Concretes a number of deficiencies have been recorded The main defects may be characteπsed as follows
• Bonding defects at coarse aggregate and reinforcement mamly evolved as highly porous zones of varying thickness
• Uneven homogeneity of the cement paste, l e vaπed porositv • Cracks, both macroscopic, e g from exposed surfaces and microscopic, e g bundles of plastic cracks internally in the concrete volume
• Uneven distribution of coarse aggregate
• Poor quality of the air void structure mainly characteπsed by low specific surface and high spacing factor • Lack of hydration of cement locally in the cement paste

These defects are caused by a vaπety of conditions in both the fresh and the hardening concrete It is the theory of the applicants that a majoπty of the deficiencies may be related to instability of modern concretes on micro- as well as macro level m combination with the commonly applied vibration technique

This is the reason why the concrete material and the concept which are the subject of the present patent claims were developed with the objective of obtaining a high degree of stability to avoid such degradation m combination with rheological properties which will lead to a self-levelling and self-compacting behaviour The innovative concrete composition shall be characteπsed by a high viscosity and low yield strength This is achieved a o. by addition of 2-10% palygorskite in combination with addition of superplasticising chemical additives
A number of other patents descπbe the use of palygorskite in concrete but the application differs from the use m our invention on the following points

The Japanese patent JP 7277795 by Denki Kagaku Kogoy KK descπbes the addition of 0 25 - 5% (of the cement wt ) of water-reducing additives in combination with 0 1 -15% of an inorganic mateπal such as bentomte, phlogopite, zeolite, carbon, coke or attapulgite in order to eliminate viscosity, reduce slump and enhance strength m concrete This deviates from our invention by referπng to a broad group of inorganic mateπals including attapulgite (palygorskite) whereas in our invention, only the particle shape of the palygorskite is considered of importance and whereas we prescπbe the use of a superplasticising additive as a prerogative for the predicted behaviour Further, the
invention claims that the use of inorganic materials aims at eliminating viscosity, whereas our invention has the objective of increasing the viscosity without increase in the yield strength.

The Japanese patent JP 7053248 from Denki Kagaku Kogyo KK describes an addition of 0.25 - 0.5% of water-reducing additives in combination with 0.1 - 15% of an inorganic material from a group consisting of bentonite, phlogopite, graphite, talc, zeolite, boron nitride, activated carbon, coal cinders, diatomaceous earth, perlite and attapulgite with the aim of reducing viscosity and prevent drying-out shrinkage in the plastic concrete, whereas in our invention only the particle shape of attapulgite in combination with supeφlasticiser is claimed to result in the desired properties. The present invention does, further, aim at increasing and not reducing the viscosity. The Japanese patent JP 6144909 from Ohbayashi Coφ. refer to application of fibrous clay minerals such as sepiolite, attapulgite and palygorsktie in combination with a cellulosic segregation reducing agent such as methyl cellulose with the aim of improving the stability of concrete. This patent deviates from our invention by using palygorskite together with and as part substitution for cellulose fibres and by using these materials without a supeφlasticiser. Further, the puφose is production of aerial concretes.

The Japanese patent JP 5238800 from Ohbayashi Coφ. applies palygorskite or sepiolite in a cement mortar to improve the strength, whereas the use of palygorskite in our invention serves a rheological puφose. Further, the use of supeφlasticiser is not prescribed in the Japanese patent.

The Japanese patent JP 64003040 from Denki Kogoyo KK describes the addition of inorganic matter selected from bentonite, phlogopite, brimstone, zeolite, activated carbon, coal cinders and attapulgite with a high-performance water-reducing agent such as polyalkylsulfonate. The aim of this patent is to improve the handling properties of concrete and to improve strength. This deviates from our invention by reference to a broad group of inorganic materials incl. palygorskite, whereas our invention only mentions palygorskite and prescribes the use of these materials in combination with a supeφlasticiser which is necessary to achieve the desired effect.

The Japanese patent JP 920293048 from Ohbayashi Coφ. refers to use of fibrous clay minerals together with cellulose polymers in order to improve the stability of concrete. This deviates from our invention by the use of palygorskite together with cellulose fibres (polymers) and by not prescribing the use of supeφlasticisers. Further, the patent does not claim the objective of producing self-levelling vibration-free concrete.

The Japanese patent JP 900058967 from Tokyo Kensetsu KK describes the use of sepiolite and palygorskite in order to improve the segregation resistance of a roller compacted concrete. Our invention does not address the RCC concept and the Japanese invention does not mention the use of palygorskite in combination with supeφlasticiser, which is not a common ingredient in RCC.

The Japanese patent JP 840094587 from Nisso Master Builders KK prescribe the use of sepiolite or attapulgite in combination with conventional plasticisers to obtain improved workability. This deviates from our invention by use of palygorskite to improve workability of ordinary plasticised concretes and not with the objective of controlling supeφlasticised, self-levelling concretes.
The Japanese patent 60255654 from Nisso Master Builders KK prescπbes the use of

105 crushed sepiolite mineral in combination with a fluidismg agent in the fluidisation of concrete. 'Pref. Sepiolite mineral is aggregate of magnesium silicate needle crystals such as attapulgite or sepiolite, etc '
Basically, sepiolite and palygorskite (often called attapulgite) both belong to the layer silicates of inverted πbbons, group sepiohte-palygorskite, but sepiolite belongs to the

110 trioctahedral subgroup and palygorskite to the dioctahedral subgroup (1) Sepiolite has the ideal formula Mg Si)2(OH2)4(H20) , while palygorskite has the ideal formula Al4Sι (OH2)4(OH)2(H2O) (2) and has, thus, 4A1 octahedral cations while sepiolite has 8Mg octahedral cations. In fact, dioctahedral layer silicates contain typically Al and tπoctahedral Mg, because of the larger size of the Mg cation compared to Al. The two

115 minerals are, thus, clearly different, and sepiolite is the Mg-contammg one. Palygorskite is predominantly needle-shaped and sepiolite most often πbbon shaped Since palygorskite is not a (tπoctahedral) magnesium silicate but instead a (dioctahedral) aluminium silicate, the patent 60255654 does not refer to the mineral palygorskite and is, thus, not in conflict with the present patent application

Whereas we do recognise that self-levelling or self-compacting concretes at present may be considered known technology, we do also maintain that these concretes are never produced by use of the combination palygorskite/supeφlasticiser and, further, that the concept of self-levelling or self-compacting concrete was first mentioned in the literature
125 m Japan 1986 (3) Consequently, none of the mentioned patents can address this topic, which was unknown at the time of the patent
State-of-the-art concretes in this field apply elongated polymers as e.g. polysacchaπdes instead of palygorskite One commonly used product is 'Velan gum' from the company Monsanto Ltd
130 The cost of this product is a magnitude higher than the predicted market pπce of palygorskite
Further, of an inorganic product like palygorskite can be added dunng production of a cement having rheology controlling properties This technique is unknown today, though it offers large advantages
Both above mentioned records underline the innovative aspects of the present invention
We have not found any patents which claim the use of a combination of palygorskite and supeφlasticiser to produce self-levelling and self-compacting concretes by means of
140 controlling (maximising) the viscosity/yield strength ratio.

The decisive part of our invention is exactly these properties and the related property 'filling capacity' This invention will cause that the previously used method of vibration to consolidate the concrete may be redundant and the deficiencies as descπbed under 'background' may be prevented
The invention is, thus, innovative and not in conflict with any known patent even though the use of palygorskite as illustrated above is not unknown

SPECIFICATION

160 The invention deals with production of self-levelling, self-compacting concrete, characterised by a high filling capacity and good stability of the cementitious microstructure achieved by adding 2-10% palygorskite measured as % by weight of the total dry binder. Particularly, the concrete is characterised by a high micro stability when exposed to high pumping pressures (100 - 200 bar), high segregation resistance and a high
165 ratio between viscosity and yield strength of the fresh concrete.
The concrete is, further, characterised by the following properties.

• flow properties are obtained by composition of the aggregates for easy flow and by use 170 of supeφlasticisers to such an extent that the concrete without palygorskite addition would reach a slump exceeding 150 mm.

• flow properties in relation to confined casting space because of dimensional reductions, reinforcement etc. are significantly improved by addition of palygorskite, which decrease the slump without affecting the yield strength.
• the paste content in the concrete is in the range 25-40%o of the concrete volume.
• the cement paste expose clear thixotropic behaviour.
• even concrete with porous, lightweight aggregates may be pumped at usual pumping pressures (<150 bar).

180 • the cement paste (the binder) is usually composed of at least three solid components in addition to palygorskite, e.g. Portland Cement, microsilica and an industrial or natural pozzolanic powder.
• the palygorskite is characterised by an aspect ratio (length/diameter ratio) >35.

185 Several tests have demonstrated that concrete produced in accordance with this invention expose a stable (high) plastic viscosity tolerating even some variation in the water content and that the rheology of the concrete - particularly the internal and external segregation tendencies - is not effected by minor variations in the water content. Consequently, the concrete could be characterised as tolerant towards variations in the
190 water content.

Three full-scale demonstrations have proven that properties like e.g. permeability, strength and adhesion to the reinforcement were very satisfying and that the concrete was stable during production and of a general high quality. 195 The full-scale structures did not expose any of the deficiencies which were described in the section 'background' and the concrete filled the structure completely.

claim.claim-text: Self-levelling, self-compacting concrete produced on the basis of Portland Cement and/or other hydraulic binders such as pozzolans with addition of water and aggregate characterised by a content of palygorskite in combination with one or more types of supeφlasticising additives.
Self-levelling, self-compacting concrete in accordance with claim no. 1, characterised by a content of palygorskite in an amount of 2 - 12% of the binder.

Self-levelling, self-compacting concrete in accordance with claim no. 1 characterised by the content of supeφlasticising additive in dry of dissolved form, e.g. sulphonated melaminformaldehyde, sulphonated naphthalene or additives of type Glenium in an amount of 2 - 15 kg/m3 depending on effect of such additives (amounts given for saturated solutions) with a dosage to obtain a slump exceeding 150 mm before addition of palygorskite.
No. 4 Self-levelling, self-compacting concrete in accordance with claim no. 1 characterised by a binder content of 300 - 450 kg binder per m3 and 0 - 10% microsilica.
Self-levelling, self-compacting concrete in accordance with claim no. 1 characterised by the use of porous aggregate.
The use of micro-stabilised concrete in accordance with claims nos. 1 - 5 for concrete structures. No. 7

Procedure for production of a self-levelling, self-compacting concrete based on Portland cement and/or other binders such as pozzolans and aggregate. The composition is characterised by the addition of one or more supeφlasticisers in combination with an addition of palygorskite. No. 8

Procedure for production of self-levelling, self-compacting concrete in accordance with claim no. 7 characterised by the addition of an amount of supeφlasticiser as claimed in claim no. 3 and addition of palygorskite in an amount of 2 - 12% of the binder. No. 9
Application of self-levelling, self-compacting concrete in accordance with claim nos. 7 and 8 for construction of concrete structures.

No. 10 Application of self-levelling, self-compacting concrete in accordance with claim nos. 1-5 or a self-levelling, self-compacting concrete produced in accordance with claim nos. 7 and 8 and using a porous aggregate; Placed in the structures by pumping.
